newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU sees 2.0 to 3.0 pct grain area rise in 1997.
newsitem.headline: EU sees 2.0 to 3.0 pct grain area rise in 1997.

text.p: The European Commission tentatively expects EU plantings for the 1997 grain harvest to increase by between two and three percent, in line with trade estimates, EU member state officials said.
The Commission and member states said it would be a couple of months before a reliable estimate could be made.
An increase is expected following a halving to five percent the amount of land farmers must set aside in 1997 in order to receive EU compensation payments.

Farmers are expected to plant more barley because this was the cereal mostly taken out of production under earlier schemes when set-aside was much higher, an official said after a discussion by EU cereal experts on Thursday.
Spain and Portugal reported problems due to heavy rain between November and March followed by dry weather since then.

The Commission's tentative estimate estimate is in line with a forecast last month by Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby, of a 2.6 percent increase to 24.77 million hectares in winter grain plantings. No new figures were circulated by the Commission.
